entries.name: NetIntel Password Breach Check
entries.description: Checks whether a password has appeared in known data breaches via the HaveIBeenPwned Pwned Passwords API using k-anonymity (only a 5-character SHA-1 hash prefix is sent — the full password never leaves the server), returning breach count, a risk level, and an A-F grade so agents can enforce password policies without storing or exposing credentials.

password.description: Password to check against known data breaches (1-500 characters; sent as a query param but only a k-anonymity SHA-1 prefix leaves the server)
Plaintext password to check — hashed locally with SHA-1; only a 5-char k-anonymity prefix leaves the server. Never stored, logged or transmitted in full.

sha1.description: Alternative input: a full 40-hex SHA-1 hash of the password (so the plaintext never leaves your side).

ntlm.description: Alternative input: a full 32-hex NTLM hash (checked against the NTLM Pwned Passwords corpus).

usage.callShape: GET https://netintel.dev/breach-check/password?password=<password> (x402, USDC on Base eip155:8453 OR Solana; no JSON body; password is a query param — only a k-anonymity SHA-1 prefix is forwarded upstream)
usage.outputShape: breached (bool), breach_count (number), risk_level (string: e.g. critical), score (number 0-100), grade (letter A-F), findings[].{rule,deduction,detail}
quirks: password is a QUERY PARAM on a GET request (no JSON body): ?password=<value>
Privacy-preserving: uses HaveIBeenPwned k-anonymity — only the first 5 chars of the password's SHA-1 hash are sent upstream; the full password never leaves netintel.dev
This host (netintel.dev) advertises TWO accepts: Base USDC (eip155:8453) AND Solana USDC — paid cleanly on Base at $0.01
Failed calls (4xx/5xx, input-validation rejections) are never charged (NetIntel agent fair-trade guarantee)
Paid probe with password=test123 returned breach_count 1383480, risk_level 'critical', grade 'F'
usage.guide: Checks whether a password has appeared in known data breaches via the HaveIBeenPwned Pwned Passwords API using k-anonymity (only a 5-character SHA-1 hash prefix is sent — the full password never leaves the server), returning breach count, a risk level, and an A-F grade so agents can enforce password policies without storing or exposing credentials. GET https://netintel.dev/breach-check/password?password=<password> (x402, USDC on Base eip155:8453 OR Solana; no JSON body; password is a query param). Output: breached, breach_count, risk_level, score, grade, findings[].{rule,deduction,detail}

entries.name: NetIntel JWT Inspector
entries.description: Decodes and inspects any JWT — extracts the header algorithm, all payload claims (issuer, subject, audience, issued-at, expiry), signature presence, and a security score/grade with findings — without requiring the signing secret, so agents can debug auth issues, check token expiry, and extract identity claims.

token.description: JWT token string (3 dot-separated segments); a 'Bearer ' prefix is stripped automatically. Query param on a GET request.

is_expired.description: null when the token has no exp claim

usage.callShape: GET https://netintel.dev/jwt-inspector/decode?token=<jwt> (x402, USDC on Base eip155:8453 OR Solana; no JSON body; token is a query param, URL-encode it)
usage.outputShape: valid_structure (bool), header{algorithm,token_type,key_id}, payload{issuer,subject,audience,expires_at,expires_at_unix,issued_at,issued_at_unix,not_before,jwt_id,custom_claims}, is_expired (bool|null), seconds_until_expiry (num|null), human_expiry (str|null), signature_hex, signature_present (bool), security_flags[], score (0-100), grade (A-F), findings[].{rule,label,impact,detail}
quirks: token is a QUERY PARAM on a GET request (no JSON body): ?token=<jwt>; URL-encode it.
A leading 'Bearer ' prefix is stripped automatically.
Decodes only — does NOT verify the signature (no secret needed); signature_present/signature_hex just report the third segment.
is_expired / seconds_until_expiry / human_expiry come back null when the token has no exp claim.
This host (netintel.dev) advertises two accepts: Base USDC (eip155:8453) AND Solana USDC — paid cleanly on Base at $0.005.
Provider is agent fair-trade: 4xx/5xx (e.g. malformed token) are never charged.
usage.guide: Decode/inspect a JWT without its secret. GET https://netintel.dev/jwt-inspector/decode?token=<url-encoded-jwt> (x402, USDC on Base eip155:8453 OR Solana; token is a query param, no JSON body). Pay $0.005 USDC. Read header.algorithm, payload claims (subject/issuer/audience/issued_at/expires_at), is_expired, and the security score/grade + findings[]. Signature is reported but NOT verified.

entries.name: Agentstools Account-Takeover Risk Assessment
entries.description: Composite account-takeover risk score (0-100) that fuses a privacy-preserving k-anonymity Pwned-Passwords exposure check with a domain's known Have I Been Pwned breach history, returning a risk category, weighted per-signal reasons, per-dimension detail and coverage so an agent can triage credential risk before accepting or reusing a login.

password.description: Plaintext password — hashed locally with SHA-1 (k-anonymity, only a 5-char prefix sent upstream); never stored, logged or transmitted

sha1.description: Alternative to password: a full 40-hex SHA-1 hash (so the plaintext never leaves your side)

ntlm.description: Alternative to password: a full 32-hex NTLM hash (MD4 not computable server-side, so send the hash for the NTLM corpus)

domain.description: Optional domain to fold in its known HIBP breach history as additional ATO signals

outputSchema.risk_category: string: minimal | low | medium | high | critical
outputSchema.password_breach_count: integer (times the password appears in breach corpora)
outputSchema.hash_prefix: string (the 5-char k-anonymity SHA-1 prefix that was sent upstream)
outputSchema.signals: object[] { signal, dimension, severity, weight, reason }

usage.callShape: POST https://api.agentstools.dev/breach/assess with a JSON body: password (plaintext — hashed locally via k-anonymity, never transmitted) OR sha1 (40-hex) OR ntlm (32-hex); plus an optional domain to fold in its HIBP breach history. x402 v2 exact, $0.01 USDC on Base (eip155:8453), no API key. Result is inline in the synchronous 200 body; no polling.
usage.outputShape: JSON: ato_risk_score (0-100), risk_category (minimal|low|medium|high|critical), password_compromised (bool), password_breach_count, hash_prefix (5-char k-anonymity prefix), reasons[], signals[]{signal,dimension,severity,weight,reason}, dimensions{password{status,compromised,breach_count,hash_prefix,hash_mode,k_anonymity}, domain{status,domain,breaches[],summary{total_breaches,total_accounts,most_recent_breach,has_password_breach,has_stealer_log,has_sensitive_data}}}, coverage{dimensions_evaluated[],password_evaluated,domain_evaluated}, source, attribution, attribution_url, disclaimer.
quirks: Body input: supply ONE of password | sha1 | ntlm (password is hashed locally with SHA-1 and only the 5-char prefix is sent upstream — plaintext never transmitted/stored/logged). domain is OPTIONAL; without it only the password dimension is scored.
Static price $0.01 (amount 10000 = 0.01 USDC, 6 decimals) — a fixed quote, not dynamic.

The score is deterministic and weighted: password prevalence drives the password signal (a password seen millions of times = trivially credential-stuffed); the domain dimension adds signals for stealer-log dumps, password-exposing breaches, highly-sensitive-data breaches, recency (<1yr) and repeated exposure. Re-rank via signals[] weights if needed.
Best-effort: an unavailable upstream is flagged in dimensions[*].status, never returned as an error.

Verified body {password:'Summer2024!', domain:'example.com'} -> ato_risk_score 22, risk_category medium, password_breach_count 3614; example.com had 0 known domain breaches, so only the password signal fired.

Credential-exposure / ATO INDICATORS only, not a guarantee: a breached password means it is unsafe to use, but a domain's breach history does NOT mean any specific account on it is compromised. Source: Have I Been Pwned (CC BY 4.0).

Distinct from siblings on this host: /breach/password (password-only compromise check), /breach/domain (a domain's known breach catalogue), /breach/account (email->breach metadata, needs a keyed HIBP subscription — returns available:false when unconfigured). This op is the composite ATO score that fuses password + domain.
usage.guide: Triage account-takeover risk for a credential in one call before accepting or reusing it. POST https://api.agentstools.dev/breach/assess with {password:'<plaintext>'} (or {sha1:'<40-hex>'} / {ntlm:'<32-hex>'} so the plaintext never leaves you), plus an optional {domain:'<domain>'} to fold in that domain's known Have I Been Pwned breach history. The password is checked with k-anonymity (hashed locally, only a 5-char SHA-1 prefix sent upstream). It is an x402 endpoint costing $0.01 USDC on Base (no API key) — pay the 402 quote and re-request; the result is inline in the synchronous 200 body. Read the headline from ato_risk_score (0-100) and risk_category (minimal|low|medium|high|critical); password_compromised + password_breach_count for the password dimension; dimensions.domain.summary + signals[]/reasons[] for what drove the score; coverage for what was evaluated. Treat as automated indicators, not a guarantee — a breached password is unsafe to reuse, but a domain's breach history does not prove any given account is compromised. Verified 2026-07-30 with {password:'Summer2024!', domain:'example.com'} -> HTTP 200, $0.01 charged, ato_risk_score 22 / medium.
